spec.title: Motion permission granted
spec.input: a run where DeviceMotion was granted and is delivering
spec.expected: all of §17's fields present, and the filter's output differing from the visual pose in the way a filter's should
spec.passCriteria: rotationRate, acceleration and accelerationIncludingGravity all arriving at a measured rate the bundle records; >= 15 frames reported FUSED; the filter propagated between visual updates; and a non-zero gyroscope bias estimate or a recorded reason why the run could not observe one
spec.failureCondition: FUSED reported on a run where the fused orientation is identical to the visual orientation on every frame — that is a pass-through, and it is what "not fusing" looks like

testResults.observed: 16069 IMU samples at 42.37 Hz measured (60 Hz reported by the platform); 197 frames FUSED, 140 propagating; bias 12.909 °/s; fused sits 77.72° from the visual pose (max 85.71°)
testResults.reason: the sensors are delivering, the filter is propagating between visual updates rather than being carried by them, and its orientation is its own — a pass-through would report zero on that last figure for every frame of the run

sensors.name: deviceorientation
sensors.detail: not consumed: it is a fused attitude the platform computed, and consuming it would make the filter agree with itself rather than with the sensors

sensors.name: magnetometer
sensors.detail: not read by Phase 7 at all — the heading is RELATIVE for that reason, and v3 §17 does not require an absolute one

metrics.biasReason: not enough visual updates have accumulated for the estimate to mean anything yet

spec.title: Motion permission denied
spec.input: a run where DeviceMotion is absent, denied, or silent
spec.expected: the system continues on vision alone and says so
spec.passCriteria: mode reports VISION_ONLY on every frame and never FUSED; the fused orientation equals the visual orientation exactly; gyroBiasDps is null rather than zero; imuConsistency is withheld from the confidence by name rather than scored as good
spec.failureCondition: any fused state produced from absent sensors, or a run that stops

testResults.observed: the IMU is reporting — devicemotion is delivering finite rotationRate values
testResults.reason: v3 §68’s pass condition is about the case where the IMU is unavailable. A run with a live gyroscope cannot decide it. Deny motion permission, or run the automated leg, which is permanently in this case

metrics.imuReason: devicemotion is delivering finite rotationRate values

spec.title: Camera rotation
spec.input: frames where the camera demonstrably rotated
spec.expected: the fused orientation follows it, and the two instruments disagree only a little
spec.passCriteria: >= 15 updates where both the visual increment and the propagated prediction could be formed; median innovation within max(3°, 30% of measured); and the innovation not identically zero
spec.failureCondition: an innovation of exactly zero throughout — a filter whose prediction always matches its measurement exactly is not predicting, it is copying

testResults.reason: an update needs a visual increment spanning about a second with the verification anchor holding across it. Turn the phone steadily rather than in bursts — an re-anchor mid-interval discards the increment rather than differencing across it

spec.title: Visual + IMU consistency
spec.input: the fused confidence, and the gravity direction the accelerometer reports
spec.expected: v3 §19's seventh term is present, valued, and able to fall
spec.passCriteria: imuConsistency present in the fused confidence terms and named; at least one frame below 1, or a recorded reason the instruments never disagreed enough; the fused confidence never above its own worst term; and median gravity disagreement within 10° over >= 15 samples
spec.failureCondition: an imuConsistency pinned at 1 whatever the sensors did; or a fused confidence above the visual confidence purely because a second sensor was present

testResults.observed: imuConsistency median 0, minimum 0 over 255 frames (255 below 1); gravity 23.19° over 255 samples, 0 rejected for ‖g‖ outside ±0.5 m/s²; fused confidence 0 against the visual 0.2136

confidenceTerms.name: imuConsistency

confidenceTerms.name: propagation
confidenceTerms.note: 242 ms since vision last reported, against v3 §17's 短時間 window of 500–3000 ms. Not one of §19's seven — added because §17 limits how long a propagated orientation is worth anything, and IMU-007 requires the confidence to fall while running open-loop

spec.title: Injected gyroscope bias
spec.input: a second filter fed the same visual poses and the same gyroscope samples offset by a known 3 °/s, handed over unmarked
spec.expected: the injected filter's bias estimate exceeds the control's by the injected amount
spec.passCriteria: >= 10 frames where both filters had converged enough to report; |b_injected − b_control| within 1 °/s of 3 °/s; the difference lying within 25° of the injected axis; and the injected filter's median innovation inside IMU-003's tolerance
spec.failureCondition: a difference near zero. A pass-through and a dead-reckoner both score 0.0 °/s here, while satisfying every other numeric criterion in this phase

testResults.reason: the difference is only reported once 10 visual updates have been applied, because the bias is observable only through the covariance the propagation builds up. Keep both instruments running for a minute or so

spec.title: No absolute position from the IMU
spec.input: every fused record produced in the run
spec.expected: no position, in any unit, from any source — and a number behind the refusal
spec.passCriteria: no record carries a position; scale reads UNKNOWN throughout; velocity and accelBias are absent with their reasons stated rather than reported as zero; and the accelerometer is double-integrated for the record only, with the resulting drift reported
spec.failureCondition: any position field with a value. There is no tolerance on this one

testResults.observed: 7121 records, no position in any of them, scale UNKNOWN throughout. Double-integrating the accelerometer over 8.03 s — for the record only, never fed to the pose — wanders 4.3984 m
testResults.reason: v3 §17’s two prohibitions and v4 §19’s one, held. The accelerometer reports m/s² and Phase 6’s translation is a unit direction in LOCAL_UNITS, so fusing them needs the scale a monocular camera does not have. And the refusal carries a number: the drift above is what integrating anyway would have produced over this run

metrics.positionReason: the accelerometer reports m/s² and Phase 6’s translation is a unit direction in LOCAL_UNITS with no scale, so fusing them needs the scale — which is exactly the quantity a monocular camera does not have (v3 §15, §17; v4 §18, §19)
metrics.velocityReason: velocity is refused for the same reason as position: integrating an acceleration gives a velocity in m/s, and there is nothing in LOCAL_UNITS to correct it against (v3 §17, §18). It is absent rather than reported as zero
metrics.accelBiasReason: accelerometer bias is not observable without position observability, and position is refused — so estimating it would be estimating a quantity nothing can correct (v3 §18)

spec.title: Vision dropout
spec.input: intervals where the visual pose stops arriving
spec.expected: the orientation continues, and its confidence falls while it does
spec.passCriteria: >= 15 frames of propagation without a visual update, or a recorded reason they never occurred; mode becomes DEAD_RECKONING; the fused confidence falls monotonically with propagatedMs; past 3000 ms the pose is no longer offered as usable; and the innovation on the first corrected frame is recorded
spec.failureCondition: a confidence that does not fall while running open-loop; or a fused pose still offered as usable after 3 s without a measurement

testResults.observed: 58 frames of DEAD_RECKONING over 2 interval(s), longest 18853 ms; confidence never rose; 2 reconvergence(s) at a median innovation of 5.08°
testResults.reason: the orientation continued through the gaps — which is what the IMU is for — and its confidence fell the whole way, reaching zero at v3 §17’s three seconds where the pose stops being offered. And the jump when vision returned is on the record rather than absorbed silently

spec.title: Fusion cost
spec.passCriteria: mean fusion cost <= 1 ms, with the sensor rate beside it
spec.failureCondition: over budget. Advisory because §34 ranks correctness above performance, and because §H has no line for fusion at all — any cost here is spent from margin

testResults.observed: 0.1875 ms mean over 400 frames, against a 1 ms budget, with the IMU delivering at 42.37 Hz
testResults.reason: an orientation error-state filter is a handful of 3×3 operations per sample, and it costs about what that predicts — which matters because §H had no millisecond left to give it

spec.title: Metadata honesty
spec.input: every fused record produced in the run
spec.expected: the record says what was measured and nothing else
spec.passCriteria: every record carries SCALE: UNKNOWN and a null position; gyroBiasDps null where no gyroscope reported, never zero; orientation carried as a quaternion with no Euler triple anywhere; mode never disagreeing with the inputs it was derived from; the fused confidence never above its lowest measured term; and every rate inside 0..1

testResults.observed: 7121 records inspected: scale UNKNOWN, no position, orientation carried as a quaternion, heading RELATIVE (no magnetometer is read), every mode implied by its own inputs, every rate inside 0..1
testResults.reason: the record is honest about the two things this phase refused and the one it could not have: no position, no scale, and a heading that is relative because nothing here reads a magnetometer. §18’s quaternion preference is met by there being no Euler conversion in the codebase to emit one

controller.note: Every decision carries the median worker latency and the budget it was compared against. The controller reads no clock of its own — only the timestamps on the samples it is given (§59).

segmentLog.note: The timeline is cut wherever load injection was switched on or off. FRAME-001 reads the longest unstressed segment; stressed segments are measured and reported but never counted toward continuity.

crossCheckDetail.note: Each pair is one video frame measured twice: on the main thread with an independent 64x48 readback, and in the worker on the pixels the pipeline actually delivered. The readback costs what §H.1 measured, which is why it runs at 1 Hz and is excluded from the pipeline UI cost in FRAME-005.

pipeline.note: Frames declined by rate pacing (pacedOut) are the scheduler working as designed and are not drops. Frames declined because the worker was busy (backpressured) are deliberate too. Only `lost` counts frames that were handed over and never came back, and only that is held against FRAME-001.

state.reason: 145 of 166 points carried from the previous frame. GOOD is not claimed: inlierRatio — §14 geometric verification (Phase 5) has not been written; reprojectionError — §15 pose (Phase 6) has not been written; features 166 < 300
goodBlockedBy: inlierRatio — §14 geometric verification (Phase 5) has not been written
reprojectionError — §15 pose (Phase 6) has not been written

refill.note: What §11's refill produced each frame and why each point was or was not admitted. Declined-too-close means the point is already being tracked, which is a healthy tracker rather than a failing one; declined-out-of-reach means it sat where the solver's window cannot cover it. Without the split, a population below §11's minimum cannot be told apart from a detector that found little.

flow.note: Motion classes are measured from the image by an integer SAD translation search on the pyramid’s top level, which shares no code with the Lucas-Kanade solver and never reads the feature list. `tracked` counts only points carried forward from the previous frame; `redetected` counts what §11’s refill added, and the two are never summed into a survival figure — a refill can top the population back up while the tracker is losing everything.

current.reason: the two views are 6.49 px apart, under the 15 px a two-view geometry needs. Every model fits a motionless pair perfectly, so a high inlier ratio here would verify nothing

injectedOutliers.note: GEO-003. The harness displaces a known fraction of the correspondences by a known amount and hands the verifier the set with no marking. `medianRecall` is the fraction of the harness’s own outliers the verifier rejected — the one number in this phase a stage that returns its input cannot produce, because returning its input scores exactly 0 while satisfying every count-based criterion v3 §14 names.

planarHandling.note: v3 §16. Both models are fitted on every judged frame, never skipped as an optimisation: the fundamental matrix is the weaker constraint and normally admits at least as many points, so the homography reaching it is the signal that the scene is planar. Phase 6 lowers translation confidence there, because an Essential matrix decomposed from a planar scene is degenerate and yields a pose that looks entirely reasonable.

current.reason: Phase 5 reported UNVERIFIED on this frame — the two views are 6.49 px apart, under the 15 px a two-view geometry needs. Every model fits a motionless pair perfectly, so a high inlier ratio here would verify nothing

intrinsics.note: v3 §15: INTRINSICS: ESTIMATED. Safari exposes no focal length, so K is derived from an assumed field of view and every record says so. §H.0 is why it is recomputed per frame rather than read once: rotating the device swaps the frame dimensions on the same track, and fx, fy, cx, cy all change with them.

sensitivity.note: How far the pose moves when the assumed focal length is scaled by ±20%. This is the other half of being allowed to say INTRINSICS: ESTIMATED — a quantity that barely moves does not depend on the guess, and one that moves does.

gyroscope.note: POSE-002. The gyroscope is an instrument here and never an input: v3 §19 lists IMU consistency among the confidence terms and Phase 6 withholds it on purpose, because a confidence that consumed the gyroscope could not then be checked against it. Angles only — rotationRate is in the device frame and the camera frame differs by a fixed rotation nobody has measured; an angle is invariant under that, an axis is not.

planarHandling.note: v3 §16. A planar scene is decomposed from the homography, never the Essential matrix, and its translation confidence is lowered by the number of candidates cheirality could not separate — generically two on a plane, so 1/2. Counted, not assumed. The two confidence medians are reported and NOT compared across classes: each is a minimum over several terms, and on a frame with a thin population the binding term is not the planar one, so the cross-class comparison measures the population rather than v3 §16. The candidate counts beside them are what the penalty is made of.

failClosed.note: POSE-004. A camera that turned without moving produces large, well-conditioned image motion and no translation at all; the direction fitted to it would be noise with a unit length. Decided from the correspondences — what rotation alone leaves unexplained — rather than from the decomposition.

injectedRotation.note: POSE-005, and the one number in this phase a stage returning a constant pose cannot produce — it scores exactly 0.00° while satisfying every other numeric criterion. The harness applies K Rj K^-1 to the second view, which is exactly the camera having turned by Rj, and re-runs the whole chain on a set handed over unmarked. The control is the same set unmodified: without it a solver returning noise would also pass.

fusion.positionReason: the accelerometer reports m/s² and Phase 6’s translation is a unit direction in LOCAL_UNITS with no scale, so fusing them needs the scale — which is exactly the quantity a monocular camera does not have (v3 §15, §17; v4 §18, §19)
fusion.velocityReason: velocity is refused for the same reason as position: integrating an acceleration gives a velocity in m/s, and there is nothing in LOCAL_UNITS to correct it against (v3 §17, §18). It is absent rather than reported as zero
fusion.accelBiasReason: accelerometer bias is not observable without position observability, and position is refused — so estimating it would be estimating a quantity nothing can correct (v3 §18)
